title: AppSec Framework adapter contract (appsec.adapter/v1alpha1)
description: The document a framework adapter writes to stdout. The Go core is the runtime authority and validates more than this schema can express — duplicate and contradictory facts, path safety, string sanitisation and size budgets. This schema exists so an adapter author in any language can validate output without reading Go, and a conformance test asserts the two agree.

contractVersion.description: The contract version, not the adapter's version. A version this build does not know is refused rather than interpreted, because a later contract may give an existing field a different meaning.

name.description: Adapter identifier. Must match the name the core invoked.

version.description: The adapter's own version, for the operator's benefit.

extractionMethod.description: How the adapter learned what it reports. The core maps this onto provenance; an adapter cannot state provenance directly. framework-native executes the inspected application's own code and requires explicit operator trust.

target.description: Best-effort description of what was inspected. Never trusted for anything security-relevant.

facts.description: Normalized security facts. Framework constructs are translated by the adapter; the core never learns what a middleware or a guard is.

path.description: Path template with parameters in {braces}. No scheme, authority, query or fragment, and no parent-directory reference: a fact about another origin must not enter this target's oracle.

value.description: Values are namespaced by kind and the core enforces the pairing. "unknown" is available to every kind and is the honest answer whenever an adapter met a construct it could not resolve.

control.description: Opaque label for the control found, such as a permission name. Never interpreted by the core.

evidence.description: Where in the application the fact came from. A location, never source contents.

file.description: Path relative to the inspected root. Absolute or escaping paths are refused.

limitations.description: What the adapter could not determine, in its own words. This is how the absence of a fact stays distinguishable from the absence of a control — without it, an adapter that could not read a construct is indistinguishable from one that found no control there.
